Student & parent journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

  2. 02Visit, demo or trial2 automations

01

Discover and enquire

Parents and students compare institutions on search, social media, review sites and word of mouth, then enquire by form, call, WhatsApp or walk-in, often in the evening and within a short admissions season.

Touchpoints

  • Search and social ads
  • Website and prospectus pages
  • Education fairs and school seminars
  • Walk-ins and phone calls
  • WhatsApp click-to-chat

Accountable owner

Admissions head or counseling lead

Automations on this stage

Discover and enquire · 3–5 weeks

Admissions enquiries, counselor follow-up and campus tours

Enquiries from ads, the website, fairs, walk-ins and WhatsApp land in one CRM with their source, get an approved acknowledgment and a named counselor, and move to a campus tour or open-day slot with reminders and post-visit follow-up.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Visit, demo or trial

Families tour the campus or attend an open day, aspirants sit a demo class, and online learners try a course before paying. Most enrollment decisions are made here, and slow follow-up loses them.

Touchpoints

  • Campus tour or open day
  • Demo class
  • Free trial or sample lesson
  • Counselor call

Accountable owner

Counseling lead or growth lead

Automations on this stage

Visit, demo or trial · 2–4 weeks

Demo class to enrollment for coaching institutes

Leads from ads, school seminars and walk-ins book a demo class, get reminders and, after attending, a counselor call informed by their demo feedback. The fee plan, installment schedule, refund policy and batch options go out in writing before any payment.

View the blueprint ↗Visit, demo or trial · 4–6 weeks

Trial activation and paid conversion for online courses

Product events show which trial learners reached their first lesson, quiz or live session. Adult learners who opted in get nudges tied to their next step, under-18 accounts get service messages to the parent only, and the growth team sees conversion by course and channel.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Apply and enroll

Applications, document checks, eligibility and counseling rounds, offers and the first fee payment. Missing documents and unclear fee or refund terms are the usual reasons a willing family stalls.

Touchpoints

  • Application form
  • Document upload and verification
  • Offer letter and fee payment
  • Anti-ragging undertaking for colleges

Accountable owner

Admissions office or registrar

Automations on this stage

Apply and enroll · 5–7 weeks

Applications, document checklists and verification for colleges

Applicants complete one form with a program and category checklist. Uploads are checked for completeness, readability and name or date mismatches, the admissions office verifies each file in a queue, and missing items trigger reminders until the seat is confirmed.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Onboard and schedule

New students receive batches or sections, timetables, LMS logins, transport routes and orientation details. Changes in the first weeks are frequent, and each one has to reach the right student and parent.

Touchpoints

  • Batch, cohort or section allocation
  • Timetable and LMS access
  • Transport route assignment
  • Orientation

Accountable owner

Academic coordinator

Automations on this stage

Onboard and schedule · 3–5 weeks

Batch and cohort allocation with schedule change notices

New students are placed in batches or live cohorts by course, center or time zone, medium and timing within capacity. Faculty availability is checked, timetables are published, and every later change reaches only the affected students and parents.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Attend and learn

Daily classes, attendance, bus journeys, homework, circulars, substitutions and questions to the office. Communication volume is highest here, and this is where safety and well-being concerns first appear.

Touchpoints

  • Attendance and late arrival
  • School bus journeys
  • Homework and circulars
  • Helpdesk questions
  • Course progress and live sessions

Accountable owner

Principal, academic head or learner success lead

Automations on this stage

Attend and learn · 3–5 weeks

Absence, late arrival and school bus alerts to parents

Students marked absent without approved leave trigger a private message to the parent by a set time, with reply buttons, and bus boarding, drop and delay updates come from RFID or attendant app events. Unresolved cases reach a staff member who calls the family.

View the blueprint ↗Attend and learn · 3–4 weeks

Circulars, homework digests and PTM booking for parents

Teachers post homework and circulars once in the ERP. Parents receive one daily digest per child in their chosen language, acknowledge consent slips with a tap, and book parent-teacher meeting slots from teachers' calendars.

View the blueprint ↗Attend and learn · 3–4 weeks

Teacher absence and substitution planner

Leave recorded before a cutoff produces a proposed substitution plan from the timetable, matching free teachers by subject and sharing extra periods fairly. The vice-principal approves it, and substitutes get their periods and lesson notes before the first bell.

View the blueprint ↗Attend and learn · 4–5 weeks

Student and learner helpdesk grounded in the handbook

Students, parents and online learners ask questions on WhatsApp, the portal or the app and get answers cited from the current handbook, fee policy, academic calendar or help center. Grievances, ragging reports and signs of distress go straight to people.

View the blueprint ↗Attend and learn · 3–5 weeks

Course progress nudges and cohort engagement

Learners who stall get a reminder tied to their next module or live session, cohorts get session and deadline reminders, and learners who stay inactive are flagged to a mentor instead of receiving more messages. Child accounts get parent-facing summaries only.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Assess and report

Unit tests, mock tests, semester exams, report cards and parent-teacher meetings. Results have to reach families accurately and privately, and a weak result needs a mentor's attention, not just a number.

Touchpoints

  • Tests and mock exams
  • Results and report cards
  • Parent-teacher meetings
  • Doubt clearing and remedial classes

Accountable owner

Examination controller or academic head

Automations on this stage

Assess and report · 5–7 weeks

Test analytics and doubt routing to faculty

Each mock test produces a private topic and time analysis against the student's own history for the student, parent and mentor. Doubts sent as photos or text are tagged by subject and chapter and queued to the right faculty, with similar solved questions attached.

View the blueprint ↗Assess and report · 3–4 weeks

Report cards and results released securely to families

Once the principal or examination controller locks results, each report card or grade card is generated and the parent or adult student is notified with a secure, expiring link. PTM booking or revaluation options follow in the same notice.

View the blueprint ↗
07

Pay, renew and stay connected

Term fees and installments, re-enrollment for the next year or course, graduation and transcripts, and alumni ties that bring referrals, mentoring and placements.

Touchpoints

  • Fee reminders and receipts
  • Re-enrollment and course renewal
  • Graduation and transcripts
  • Alumni events and mentoring

Accountable owner

Accounts officer and alumni relations lead

Automations on this stage

Pay, renew and stay connected · 2–3 weeks

Respectful fee reminders, payment links and receipts

Fee payers receive courteous reminders before and after due dates with a UPI payment link, receipts arrive instantly, and installment, concession or refund requests go to the accounts office. Reminders never reach children, class groups or noticeboards.

View the blueprint ↗Pay, renew and stay connected · 2–4 weeks

Alumni directory, events and mentoring

Graduating students opt in to the alumni network, profiles are refreshed by a short annual form, event invitations go to relevant batches and cities, and mentor matches between alumni and current students are approved by the alumni office.

View the blueprint ↗

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Admissions enquiries, counselor follow-up and campus toursDiscover and enquireCounselors make every follow-up call and record outcomes, and the admissions head approves templates, answer content and assignment rules. The workflow never screens or ranks children or parents, and seats under RTE Section 12(1)(c) follow the state's own portal and process.
Demo class to enrollment for coaching institutesVisit, demo or trialCounselors hold every enrollment conversation, and the center head approves any discount or installment change. The academic head and the institute's legal adviser approve all templates so that none promises selections, ranks or assured results.
Trial activation and paid conversion for online coursesVisit, demo or trialThe growth lead approves every sequence, cap and template, and the data protection contact approves the age gate and parent consent flow. Refund and cancellation disputes go to the learner success lead, never to an automated reply.
Applications, document checklists and verification for collegesApply and enrollAdmissions officers verify every document and decide eligibility, category and seat allocation; extraction only drafts. Originals are verified in person and returned at once, as UGC requires, and withdrawals and refunds follow the UGC fee refund policy with the registrar's approval.
Batch and cohort allocation with schedule change noticesOnboard and scheduleThe academic coordinator approves every placement, batch transfer and timetable change, and faculty confirm their availability. Requests to move a student between batches are decided by the academic head, never by the scheduler.
Absence, late arrival and school bus alerts to parentsAttend and learnA named staff member phones every family that did not know about an absence, and the transport in-charge handles every missed drop or unusual delay by phone. Absence patterns are reviewed by the counselor or coordinator and never trigger automatic action.
Circulars, homework digests and PTM booking for parentsAttend and learnClass teachers approve their digests, a fluent teacher approves each translation, and the principal approves every school-wide circular and any message about safety, discipline or an incident. Parents' replies raising a concern go to the class teacher, not to an automated answer.
Teacher absence and substitution plannerAttend and learnThe vice-principal or academic coordinator approves every plan and can override any assignment. Leave approval stays with the principal or HR under the staff leave policy; the planner never approves or rejects leave.
Student and learner helpdesk grounded in the handbookAttend and learnThe dean of students or learner success lead owns the sensitive-message rules and the staffed queue. Ragging reports go to the Anti-Ragging Committee and grievances to the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee; fee waivers, discipline and academic exceptions are decided only by the authorized office.
Course progress nudges and cohort engagementAttend and learnMentors decide whom to call and what support to offer, and the learning lead approves caps and wording. Extensions, deferrals and refunds are decided by the learner success lead under the published policy.
Test analytics and doubt routing to facultyAssess and reportFaculty answer every doubt and approve any drafted hint before it reaches a student. Mentors decide on counseling or extra classes, and any sign of stress or distress goes to the institute's counselor, never to an automated message.
Report cards and results released securely to familiesAssess and reportThe principal or examination controller locks results and approves release, and teachers own their remarks. Revaluation, grace marks and any hold on a result are decided only by the examination office under the institution's rules, never by the workflow.
Respectful fee reminders, payment links and receiptsPay, renew and stay connectedThe accounts officer decides installment plans, concessions and refunds, and the principal or registrar approves reminder wording and frequency. Any step that affects a student's classes, exams or results is a management decision under the institution's policy and the law, never automated.
Alumni directory, events and mentoringPay, renew and stay connectedThe alumni relations officer approves every campaign, introduction and mentor match, and current students choose whether to accept a mentor. Directory details are shown to other alumni only where each person chose to share them.
